Q: How to use mage.exe for (re)signing manifests with Azure Trusted Code Signing A:

From https://solutionfall.com/question/can-azure-trusted-signing-be-used-to-sign-manifest-files-with-or-without-mageexe/ i get:

"Azure Trusted Signing cannot be used to sign Manifest files directly, whether with or without Mage.exe. Azure Trusted Signing is designed specifically for signing software artifacts such as executables, libraries, and container images stored in Azure services. It provides an extra layer of security and trust by verifying the authenticity and integrity of the signed artifacts. Manifest files, on the other hand, are typically used for ClickOnce deployments and do not fall under the scope of Azure Trusted Signing. If you need to sign Manifest files, you should use tools like Mage.exe or SignTool.exe, which are specifically designed for signing ClickOnce manifests."

I research the way with a Zertifcate stored in Azure-KeyVault. In https://github.com/dotnet/sign you can read supported FileTypes: ClickOnce .application and .vsto (via Mage).

But the referenced notes missing the point with mage.

So currently i check out https://www.davici.nl/clickonce-signing-from-azure-devops-via-azure-key-vault/ to sign my office addin.

Q: How to paginate Django with other get variables? A:

From Django 5.1 onwards there is a built-in template tag called querystring to solve this problem. This tag updates the provided QueryDict (defaults to request.GET) with the provided parameters and renders the formatted query string for it.

It can be used as follows:

<a href="{% querystring page=paginator.next_page_number %}">next</a>

Note: To pass request.GET by default to the tag either the django.template.context_processors.request context processor should be enabled or request should be added explicitly to the template's context.

Q: VS CODE terminal cannot use proxy A:

As far as I know, you need to start VS Code from the terminal after setting a manual proxy in the system settings. In this case, the proxy will take effect. If you launch VS Code by clicking the desktop icon, the proxy will not be applied. This bug is still exist referring to the link.

Q: Can I use my keyboard for touch instead of my mouse on android studio A:

The feature you request would have to be built into the emulator - translating keyboard input to touch inptu before it hits the target Android software. Since you're saying "on android studio" I'm assuming you refer to the AVD Android Studio Emulator. I am pretty sure that emulator does not support the feature you request, nor have I heard of any other that supports it.
